question:
Which of the following taxes was related to the land revenue (tax on agricultural land) system of the Delhi sultanate?

[CONSTABLE EXE 2023]
options: Khams
Zakat
Kharaj
Jizya
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kharaj

Explanation:
In the land revenue system of the Delhi Sultanate, Kharaj was a major tax imposed on agricultural land. It was typically a fixed portion (usually 1/3 to 1/2) of the produce and could be collected in cash or kind. The purpose was to ensure state revenue. Sultans like Alauddin Khilji and Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq made this tax system more stringent. Kharaj, under Islamic law, was originally a tax on non-Muslim farmers, but the Delhi Sultanate applied it universally.

Extra Facts:
Other significant taxes in the Delhi Sultanate included Zakat (religious tax on Muslims), Jizya (tax on non-Muslims), and Khams (1/5th of war booty). Alauddin Khilji brought land revenue under direct state control and enforced strict collections. Muhammad bin Tughlaq increased taxes, leading to peasant revolts.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कर दिल्ली सल्तनत की भू-राजस्व (कृषि भूमि पर कर) प्रणाली से संबंधित था ?

[CONSTABLE EXE 2023]
options_hi: ख़म्स
ज़कात
ख़राज
जिज्य
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है ख़राज

Explanation:
दिल्ली सल्तनत की भू-राजस्व प्रणाली में ख़राज एक प्रमुख कर था, जो कृषि भूमि पर लगाया जाता था। यह कर उपज का एक निश्चित हिस्सा (आमतौर पर 1/3 से 1/2) होता था और इसे नकद या फसल के रूप में वसूला जाता था। इसका उद्देश्य सल्तनत की आय को सुनिश्चित करना था। अलाउद्दीन खिलजी और गयासुद्दीन तुगलक जैसे सुल्तानों ने इस कर प्रणाली को और अधिक कठोर बनाया। ख़राज इस्लामिक कानून के अनुसार गैर-मुस्लिम किसानों से लिया जाने वाला कर था, लेकिन दिल्ली सल्तनत में इसे सभी किसानों पर लागू किया गया।

Extra Facts:
दिल्ली सल्तनत में अन्य महत्वपूर्ण करों में जकात (मुसलमानों पर धार्मिक कर), जिज्या (गैर-मुस्लिमों पर लगाया गया कर), और ख़म्स (लूट का 1/5 हिस्सा) शामिल थे। अलाउद्दीन खिलजी ने भू-राजस्व को सीधे राज्य के नियंत्रण में ले लिया और किसानों से सख्ती से वसूली की। मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक ने करों को बढ़ाकर किसानों में असंतोष पैदा किया, जिससे कई विद्रोह हुए।

question:
What was Iltutmish's relation with Qutubuddin Aibak?

[CONSTABLE EXE 2023]
options: son-in-law
brother
brother-in-law
son
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is son-in-law

Explanation:
Iltutmish was the son-in-law of Qutubuddin Aibak. Qutubuddin Aibak married his daughter to Iltutmish. Iltutmish was a significant ruler of the Delhi Sultanate who reigned from 1211 to 1236 CE. He succeeded Qutubuddin Aibak and strengthened the Sultanate. He introduced the Chalisa system (Turkan-i-Chihalgani) and organized the Iqta system.

Extra Facts:
Qutubuddin Aibak was the first ruler of the Delhi Sultanate and ruled from 1206 to 1210 CE. After his death, his son Aram Shah ascended the throne but proved incompetent. Iltutmish deposed him and stabilized the Delhi Sultanate.

question_hi:
इल्तुतमिश का कुतुबुद्दीन ऐबक से क्या संबंध था?

[CONSTABLE EXE 2023]
options_hi: दामाद
भाई
बहनोई
पुत्र
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है दामाद

Explanation:
इल्तुतमिश, कुतुबुद्दीन ऐबक का दामाद था। कुतुबुद्दीन ऐबक ने अपनी पुत्री का विवाह इल्तुतमिश से किया था। इल्तुतमिश दिल्ली सल्तनत का एक महत्वपूर्ण शासक था जिसने 1211 से 1236 ईस्वी तक शासन किया। वह कुतुबुद्दीन ऐबक का उत्तराधिकारी बना और उसने सल्तनत को मजबूत किया। उसने चालीसा प्रथा (तुर्कान-ए-चिहलगानी) की शुरुआत की और इक्ता प्रणाली को व्यवस्थित किया।

Extra Facts:
कुतुबुद्दीन ऐबक दिल्ली सल्तनत का पहला शासक था और उसने 1206 से 1210 ईस्वी तक शासन किया। उसकी मृत्यु के बाद उसका पुत्र आरामशाह गद्दी पर बैठा, लेकिन वह अयोग्य साबित हुआ। इल्तुतमिश ने उसे हटाकर सत्ता संभाली और दिल्ली सल्तनत को स्थिर किया।

question:
Which officer under Alauddin Khilji was required to maintain a register of merchants to ensure an adequate supply of goods?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Nazir
Rais Parwana
Muhtasib
Shahna-i-Mandi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Shahna-i-Mandi

Explanation:
Alauddin Khilji (1296-1316 CE) implemented significant economic reforms during his reign. He established the 'Diwan-i-Riyasat' (Commerce Department) and assigned the Shahna-i-Mandi (Market Superintendent) the responsibility of maintaining a register of merchants. This was aimed at ensuring adequate supply of goods, price control, and preventing black-marketing. Alauddin introduced a 'regulated market system', where merchants could trade only after registering with Shahna-i-Mandi. This system was crucial for the economic stability of the Delhi Sultanate.

Extra Facts:
Alauddin Khilji enforced a price control policy, fixing rates for grains, textiles, horses, etc. He strengthened the spy network (Barid) to monitor market malpractices. Hoarding was strictly prohibited. These reforms were essential to manage Mongol invasions and military expenditures.

question_hi:
माल की पर्याप्त आपूर्ति सुनिश्चित करने हेतु अलाउद्दीन खिलजी के अधीन किस अधिकारी के लिए व्यापारियों का रजिस्टर बनाए रखना आवश्यक था?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: नज़ीर
रईस परवाना
मुहतसिब
शहना-ए-मंडी
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है शहना-ए-मंडी

Explanation:
अलाउद्दीन खिलजी (1296-1316 ई.) ने अपने शासनकाल में कई महत्वपूर्ण आर्थिक सुधार किए। उसने 'दीवान-ए-रियासत' (वाणिज्य विभाग) की स्थापना की और शहना-ए-मंडी (बाजार निरीक्षक) को व्यापारियों का रजिस्टर बनाए रखने का दायित्व सौंपा। इसका उद्देश्य बाजार में माल की पर्याप्त आपूर्ति सुनिश्चित करना, मूल्य नियंत्रण करना और कालाबाजारी रोकना था। अलाउद्दीन ने 'नियमित बाजार प्रणाली' लागू की, जिसमें सभी व्यापारियों को शहना-ए-मंडी के पंजीकरण के बाद ही व्यापार करने की अनुमति थी। यह प्रणाली दिल्ली सल्तनत की आर्थिक स्थिरता के लिए महत्वपूर्ण थी।

Extra Facts:
अलाउद्दीन खिलजी ने मूल्य नियंत्रण नीति लागू की, जिसमें अनाज, कपड़ा और घोड़ों आदि की कीमतें तय की गईं। उसने गुप्तचर प्रणाली (बरिद) को मजबूत किया ताकि बाजारों में धोखाधड़ी की जानकारी मिल सके। स्टॉक होर्डिंग (जमाखोरी) पर सख्त प्रतिबंध लगाया गया। ये सुधार मंगोल आक्रमणों और सैन्य खर्चों को पूरा करने के लिए आवश्यक थे।

question:
Which of the following mosques/masjids was built during the reign of Lodi dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?

[SSC CPO 2023]
options: Begumpuri mosque, Delhi
Quwwat al-Islam, Delhi
Lal Masjid, Delhi
Moth ki Masjid, Delhi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Moth ki Masjid, Delhi

Explanation:
Moth ki Masjid was built during the reign of the Lodi dynasty (1451-1526 CE) of the Delhi Sultanate. This mosque was constructed by Miyan Bhua , a minister under Sikandar Lodi . It is an excellent example of the architectural style of the Lodi dynasty, the last ruling dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. The mosque's construction began with a single moth (lentil) grain , which Sikandar Lodi received from a farmer and planted. The revenue generated from its harvest was used to build this mosque.

Extra Facts:
The Lodi dynasty constructed several significant buildings, including the Shish Gumbad and Bara Gumbad . This Pashtun-origin dynasty further developed Islamic architecture in India. After the Lodis, the Mughal Empire was established, which introduced new dimensions to Indian architecture.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी मस्जिद दिल्ली सल्तनत के लोदी वंश के शासनकाल में बनाई गई थी?

[SSC CPO 2023]
options_hi: बेगमपुरी मस्जिद, दिल्ली
कुव्वत अल-इस्लाम, दिल्ली
लाल मस्जिद, दिल्ली
मोठ की मस्जिद, दिल्ली
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है मोठ की मस्जिद, दिल्ली

Explanation:
मोठ की मस्जिद को लोदी वंश के शासनकाल (1451-1526 ईस्वी) में बनवाया गया था। यह मस्जिद सिकंदर लोदी के शासनकाल में उनके मंत्री मियां भुआ द्वारा बनवाई गई थी। यह दिल्ली सल्तनत के अंतिम शासकीय वंश, लोदी वंश की वास्तुकला का एक उत्कृष्ट उदाहरण है। इस मस्जिद का निर्माण एक मोठ (दाल) के दाने से प्रारंभ हुआ था, जिसे सिकंदर लोदी ने एक किसान से प्राप्त किया था और उसे बोने के लिए दिया था। इससे प्राप्त आय से इस मस्जिद का निर्माण करवाया गया।

Extra Facts:
लोदी वंश ने दिल्ली सल्तनत में कई महत्वपूर्ण इमारतों का निर्माण करवाया, जिनमें शिश गुंबद और बड़ा गुंबद भी शामिल हैं। यह वंश पठान मूल का था और इसने भारत में इस्लामी वास्तुकला को और विकसित किया। लोदी वंश के बाद मुगल साम्राज्य की स्थापना हुई, जिसने भारतीय वास्तुकला को नए आयाम दिए।

question:
Sultan Mahmud came to India from which of the following cities of Afghanistan?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Ghazni
Jalalabad
Kabul
Kandahar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ghazni

Explanation:
Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni, also known as Mahmud Ghazni, came to India from the city of Ghazni in Afghanistan. He was the ruler of the Ghaznavid Empire (997-1030 CE) and invaded India 17 times. His primary objective was to plunder wealth, especially from temples like the Somnath Temple (1025 CE). Ghazni was his capital, and from there, he planned his military campaigns. His invasions laid the foundation for Turk-Afghan rule in India.

Extra Facts:
Mahmud Ghazni patronized scholars like Firdausi, who wrote the 'Shahnameh'. He developed Ghazni as a cultural center. His invasions promoted Islamic influence in India, though he did not establish permanent rule. His army used elephants and cavalry extensively.

question_hi:
सुल्तान महमूद अफगानिस्तान के निम्नलिखित में से किस शहर से भारत आया था?

जलालाबाद
काबुल
कांधार
solution_hi:

Explanation:

Extra Facts:
Iltutmish introduced the Iqta system, which strengthened military and administrative organization. He issued silver Tanka and copper Jital coins, forming the basis of the Delhi Sultanate's currency system. question:
Qutub-ud-din Aibak founded which of the following dynasties?

[SSC MTS ]
options: Tughluq Dynasty
Sayyid Dynasty
Khilji Dynasty
Slave Dynasty
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Slave Dynasty

Explanation:
Qutub-ud-din Aibak founded the Slave Dynasty (Mamluk Dynasty) in 1206 CE. He was a trusted slave of Muhammad Ghori and became the first Muslim ruler in India. He laid the foundation of the Delhi Sultanate and initiated the construction of the Qutub Minar, which was later completed by Iltutmish. Aibak was also known as 'Lakh Baksh' (Giver of Lakhs) due to his generosity.

Extra Facts:
The Slave Dynasty was the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, ruling from 1206 to 1290 CE. Its prominent rulers included Iltutmish, Razia Sultan, and Balban. Iltutmish strengthened the sultanate and introduced the silver Tanka (currency). Razia Sultan became the first and only female ruler of Delhi.

question:
The Iqta system was introduced by _________ in Delhi sultanate in institutional form.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Aram Shah
Gayasuddin balban
Iltutmish
Qutb-ud-din Aibak
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Iltutmish

Explanation:
The Iqta system was institutionalized in the Delhi Sultanate by Iltutmish (1211-1236 CE). It was a land revenue system where the Sultan granted land (Iqta) to military officers and administrators in exchange for their services. This system strengthened the administrative framework of the Sultanate and ensured centralized control. Iltutmish refined the system, making revenue collection and military management more efficient.

Extra Facts:
The Iqta system was originally practiced by the Seljuk Turks and was adapted by Iltutmish to suit Indian conditions. Under this system, the Iqtadar (land grantee) was responsible for revenue collection and military service. This system later evolved into the Jagirdari system during the Mughal era.

question:
Which ruler wanted to build the Alai Minar near the Qutub Minar, but could not complete it?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Ala-ud-Din Khilji

Iltutmish
Raziya Sultan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ala-ud-Din Khilji

Explanation:
Ala-ud-Din Khilji (1296-1316 CE), an ambitious ruler of the Khilji dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, initiated the construction of the Alai Minar near the Qutub Minar. He intended to build it twice as tall as the Qutub Minar as a symbol of his victories and power. However, the project remained incomplete after his death. Ala-ud-Din also built the Alai Darwaza in the Qutub complex, an excellent example of Indo-Islamic architecture.

Extra Facts:
Ala-ud-Din Khilji implemented the market control system (Diwan-i-Riyasat) to regulate prices. He successfully repelled Mongol invasions and expanded his empire to South India. During his reign, scholars and generals like Amir Khusrau and Malik Kafur played significant roles.

question:
Which was the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options: Mamluk dynasty
Tughlaq dynasty
Khilji dynasty

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mamluk dynasty

Explanation:
The first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate was the Mamluk dynasty (1206-1290 CE), also known as the 'Slave dynasty'. It was founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1206 CE after the death of his master, Muhammad Ghori. This Turkic-origin dynasty laid the foundation of Muslim rule in India. Notable rulers of this dynasty include Iltutmish, Razia Sultana, and Balban.

Extra Facts:
The construction of the Qutub Minar was started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by Iltutmish. Razia Sultana was the first and only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate (1236-1240 CE). Balban introduced the 'Blood and Iron' policy to strengthen the Sultan's authority.

question:
Who started the practice of ‘sijda’ in India?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Iltutmish
Qutubuddin Aibak
Razia Sultana
Ghiyas-ud-din Balban
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ghiyas-ud-din Balban

Explanation:
The practice of 'sijda' (prostration) was introduced in India by Ghiyas-ud-din Balban (1266-1286 CE), a Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate. This Persian custom required courtiers to kneel and bow their heads (sijda) before the Sultan. Balban used this practice to establish his authority as a 'divine ruler' and enforced strict court rituals to elevate the Sultan's dignity. He followed the 'Blood and Iron' policy to maintain control and crushed rebellions ruthlessly.

Extra Facts:
Balban promoted Persian culture to counter the influence of Turkish nobles. He abolished the 'Chalisa' (Group of Forty) and centralized power. He defended the Sultanate against Mongol invasions (Hulagu Khan) and suppressed the Bengal revolt. His reign marked the decline of the Slave Dynasty.

question:
Who was the Sultan of Delhi at the time of the establishment of Vijayanagara Empire?

Iltutmish
Mohammad bin Tughlaq
Alauddin Khilji
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mohammad bin Tughlaq

Explanation:
The Vijayanagara Empire was established in 1336 CE . At that time, the Delhi Sultanate was ruled by Mohammad bin Tughlaq (1325-1351 CE). He is known as the 'Mad Sultan' due to his controversial decisions, such as shifting the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad and introducing token currency (copper coins) . The Vijayanagara Empire was founded by Harihara and Bukka , who were earlier subordinates of the Tughlaq Empire.

Extra Facts:
The Vijayanagara Empire was a prominent Hindu kingdom in South India that ruled until the 17th century. Its capital was Hampi , a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The empire declined after the Battle of Talikota (1565) , where it was defeated by the combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates.

question:
Which of the following Sultans of Delhi adopted the policy of Blood and Iron ?

solution:

Ghiyasuddin Balban (1266-1286 CE) was a prominent Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate who adopted the 'Policy of Blood and Iron'. This policy was based on military strength and harsh suppression, aimed at crushing rebellions and maintaining law and order in the empire. Balban introduced practices like 'Sijda' (prostration) and 'Paibos' (kissing the feet) to elevate the Sultan's status to a divine level. He weakened the influence of the 'Turkan-i-Chihalgani' (The Forty) and strengthened centralized rule.

Extra Facts:
Balban defended the Sultanate from Mongol invasions and constructed forts to secure border regions. He developed an espionage network to preempt rebellions. His reign is known for militarism and despotism in the Delhi Sultanate.

Explanation:
Razia Sultan, also known as Razia al-Din, became the first and only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. She was the daughter of Sultan Iltutmish and ascended the throne in 1236 CE. Iltutmish had appointed Razia as his successor, recognizing her capabilities over his incompetent sons. However, the Turkish nobles refused to accept a female ruler and initially placed her brother, Ruknuddin Firuz, on the throne. After Ruknuddin's ineffective rule, Razia seized power in 1236 CE. During her reign, she implemented several reforms but faced opposition from the nobles, leading to her assassination in 1240 CE.

Extra Facts:
Razia Sultan broke gender norms by dressing like a man and holding open court sessions, a revolutionary act for her time. She appointed officials based on merit, disregarding caste or gender. Her reign saw the expansion of the Delhi Sultanate and emphasis on administrative reforms. Although her rule lasted only four years (1236-1240 CE), she left an indelible mark in history as a trailblazing female monarch.

महमूद गज़नवी ने 1025 ईस्वी में सोमनाथ मंदिर पर आक्रमण किया, जो उसका पंजाब के बाहर अंतिम आक्रमण था। यह मंदिर गुजरात के काठियावाड़ क्षेत्र में स्थित था और हिंदू धर्म के प्रमुख तीर्थस्थलों में से एक था। महमूद गज़नवी ने इस मंदिर को लूटा और नष्ट कर दिया, जिससे उसे भारी धन-संपदा प्राप्त हुई। यह आक्रमण उसकी भारत पर 17 बार की लूटपाट की श्रृंखला का हिस्सा था। महमूद गज़नवी के इन आक्रमणों का मुख्य उद्देश्य धन लूटना और इस्लाम का प्रसार करना था, न कि स्थायी साम्राज्य स्थापित करना।

Extra Facts:
महमूद गज़नवी ने भारत पर पहला आक्रमण 1000 ईस्वी में किया था। उसने मुख्य रूप से पंजाब, मथुरा, कन्नौज और सोमनाथ जैसे समृद्ध शहरों को निशाना बनाया। उसका सबसे प्रसिद्ध आक्रमण सोमनाथ पर था, जहाँ उसने मंदिर को नष्ट कर दिया और उसके खजाने को लूट लिया। महमूद गज़नवी की मृत्यु 1030 ईस्वी में हुई, और उसके बाद गज़नी साम्राज्य का पतन शुरू हो गया।

question:
Who invaded India during the rule of Tughlaq Dynasty?

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options: Timur
Chengiz Khan
Muhammad Ghori
Mahmud of Ghazni
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Timur

Explanation:
During the reign of the Tughlaq Dynasty (1320-1414 CE), Timur invaded India in 1398 CE. This invasion took place during the rule of Tughlaq Sultan Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah. Timur plundered Delhi and several parts of northern India, causing massive destruction. His invasion exposed the weakness of the Tughlaq Empire and became a major reason for its decline.

Extra Facts:
Timur was a powerful Central Asian ruler who founded the 'Timurid Empire'. His invasion of India was primarily aimed at looting wealth. He carried out brutal massacres in Delhi and took thousands of people as captives. This attack further weakened the Turk-Afghan rule in India.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से किसने तुगलक वंश के शासन काल में भारत पर आक्रमण किया था?

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options_hi: तैमूर
चंगेज़ खान
मुहम्मद गौरी
गजनी का महमूद
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है तैमूर

Explanation:
तुगलक वंश के शासनकाल (1320-1414 ईस्वी) में 1398 ईस्वी में तैमूर ने भारत पर आक्रमण किया था। यह आक्रमण तुगलक सुल्तान नासिरुद्दीन महमूद शाह के समय हुआ था। तैमूर ने दिल्ली सहित उत्तरी भारत के कई हिस्सों को लूटा और बड़े पैमाने पर विनाश किया। उसका यह आक्रमण तुगलक साम्राज्य की कमजोरी को उजागर करता है और इसके पतन का एक प्रमुख कारण बना।

Extra Facts:
तैमूर मध्य एशिया का एक शक्तिशाली शासक था, जिसने 'तैमूर साम्राज्य' की स्थापना की। उसका भारत पर आक्रमण मुख्यतः धन लूटने के उद्देश्य से था। उसने दिल्ली में भीषण नरसंहार किया और हज़ारों लोगों को बंदी बना लिया। यह आक्रमण भारत में तुर्क-अफ़गान शासन की नींव को और कमजोर कर दिया।
